content.text: @instructure/ui@11.7.4 just released and it includes security vulnerabilities, so we need to update, however it includes multiple other component changes since 11.7.3 and we need an upgrade strategy that includes updated the deprecation set, removing deprecated elements, updating the color/size/etc. normalization, and validating/remapping/updating the token map for new tokens / dangling refs / etc.  This should be a foundational, comprenensive update strategy for instructure/ui so that 11.7.5 and 11.8.0 can be somewhat automated, or surface points of manual intervention in a semi-automated way.  This should also be reusable so we can start marking version support and compatibility layers for consumers (i.e. Wordpress, Angular, Vitepress...)
I'll research how pantoken currently consumes `@instructure/ui`, how the token map and normalization work, and what upgrade/automation machinery already exists. Let me launch parallel exploration.

1	# Architecture overview
2	
3	pantoken resolves Instructure UI's design tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then turns
4	that single model into many small, individually-publishable packages — plain CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus,
5	React/Vue/Svelte/Angular, Tailwind/Panda/PostCSS, native Swift/Kotlin/Compose/Flutter, WordPress,
6	Drupal, Figma, and more. You install the smallest package that fits, or the unified `pantoken` meta
7	package that re-exports them all.
8	
9	## The pipeline
10	
11	`@pantoken/core` (the transformer) resolves the Tokens Studio graph into a canonical,
12	`@property`-aligned `Token[]` IR — icons rolled in as `<image>` tokens. `@pantoken/tokens` vendors
13	that IR plus the raw JSON as static files. Every emitter (`css`, `icons`, `astro`, `rehype`,
14	`swift`, and the rest) consumes the vendored IR. The native path runs `core.toStyleDictionary()`
15	→ `@pantoken/sd-config` (Style Dictionary v5) → `@pantoken/swift` / `@pantoken/cli`.
16	
17	## The upstream-decoupling constraint (the load-bearing rule)
18	
19	`@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` is GitHub-only — no npm publish, no types. `@pantoken/core`
20	depends on it. So a package that depended on `core` would transitively pull the GitHub-only upstream
21	into every consumer's install. To prevent that:
22	
23	- Type contracts live in a zero-dependency **`@pantoken/model`**.
24	- Web and emitter packages depend on **`model` + `tokens`** (both upstream-free), **never on `core`**.
25	- `core` carries an ambient `declare module "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens"` shim, since the
26	  upstream ships no types.
27	
28	When you add a package, keep it off `core` unless it genuinely runs the transform. Reach for `model`
29	(types) and `tokens` (the vendored IR) instead.
30	
31	## Workspace layout — organized by how you consume each package
32	
33	The axis is consumption, not language. The rule of thumb: **import the output → `formats/`;
34	generate it into another ecosystem → `platforms/`.**
35	
36	| Bucket       | What lives here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
37	| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
38	| `packages/`  | Core machinery: `model` (types, zero-dep), `core` (transformer), `utils` (shared resolver + drift helpers), `plugin-kit` (the plugin factory), `cli`, and `pantoken` (the auto-generated meta package).                                                                  |
39	| `formats/`   | Importable npm serializations of the IR — `tokens`, `css`, `icons`, `dtcg`, `scss`, `less`, `stylus`, `icon-font`, and `components`. You `npm i` and import these.                                                                                                       |
40	| `platforms/` | Foreign-ecosystem source you _generate_ via the CLI and publish to that ecosystem's registry — `swift`, `android`, `compose`, `flutter`, `wordpress`, `vanilla`, `drupal`, `jekyll`, `hugo`, `email`.                                                                    |
41	| `renderers/` | Integrations that produce UI — `web-components`, `react`/`vue`/`svelte`/`angular` wrappers, `react-markdown`, `rehype`, `astro`, `pendo`, and CSS-var bridges (`shadcn`, `bootstrap`, `docusaurus`, `vitepress`).                                                        |
42	| `bundlers/`  | Build-pipeline integrations — `vite`, `tailwind`, `postcss`, `next`, `webpack`, `panda`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
43	| `design/`    | Design-tool assets — `figma` (Variables payload) and `swatches` (ASE/GPL/sketchpalette).                                                                                                                                                                                 |
44	| `plugins/`   | Split by kind: `plugins/pantoken/*` are `PantokenPlugin`s (colors, focus/simple-icons/stacking/transition/visual-debug/primitives/logos); `plugins/postcss/*` are PostCSS plugins (prune-custom-props); `plugins/typedoc/*` and `plugins/vite/*` are docs/build tooling. |
45	| `tools/`     | Internal build tooling — `sd-config` (Style Dictionary, powers the native targets), `aggregate` (builds the meta package).                                                                                                                                               |
46	| `ai/`        | Consumer-facing agent assets (`@pantoken/ai`, `pantoken-ai`) — NOT for developing pantoken itself. It drops AGENTS.md, llms.txt, and editor rules into a _consumer_ repo.                                                                                                |
47	
48	## The meta package
49	
50	`pantoken` is auto-generated by `tools/aggregate`, which scans each package's
51	`"pantoken": { key, kind }` field. `kind` decides how a package joins the meta:
52	
53	- `namespace` — eager barrel + subpath.
54	- `sideEffect` — barrel + an `/inject` subpath.
55	- `subpath` — subpath only, kept **out** of the eager barrel. Used for heavy React integrations (e.g.
56	  `react-markdown`, tailwind, panda) so `import "pantoken"` never pulls React or a build config.
57	
58	`aggregate` only _writes_ the meta. When you remove a package from the meta, delete its orphaned
59	`packages/pantoken/src/<name>.ts` by hand — aggregate won't.
60	
61	## Shared helpers
62	
63	`@pantoken/utils` (deps: `model` + `arkregex`) holds the formerly copy-pasted resolver:
64	`makeResolver(base, {mode?, overrides?})` (a `var()` + `light-dark()` resolver) and `resolveTokens`,
65	plus the typed `VAR_RE`/`LIGHT_DARK_RE` regexes, `camelCase`, and `parseHexColor`. It also holds the
66	drift/validation harness — `unknownReferences(text, ir)` (bridge targets must be real tokens) and
67	`danglingReferences(css)` (self-containment: every `var()` has a definition in the same output) — plus
68	the generic token→class engines `colorUtilitiesCss` and `tokenUtilitiesCss`. `utils` must never import
69	from `components` (it sits below it). `checkPlugins` (the capability guard) lives in `plugin-kit`, not
70	`utils`.
71	
72	## The gate
73	
74	`pnpm run ready` must pass — a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`) that builds once, then fans out `vp check`,
75	test `-r`, CSS/JS lint, generated-output validation, and markdown lint concurrently. `pnpm run
76	check:publish` runs the publish gate (repository metadata + publint + attw). The same checks run on
77	every PR via `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Generated artifacts (`platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
78	`platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, web-components `src/generated/`) are
79	gitignored and reproduced on build.
80	
81	## Deliberate boundaries
82	
83	- **canvas-ios and canvas-android get no dedicated targets** — both already self-generate from InstUI
84	  through their own Style Dictionary pipelines. pantoken's generic swift/android/compose cover the
85	  general native case; duplicating their in-repo scripts would drift.
86	- **Storybook is a renderer, not a design tool** — pantoken themes the Storybook _app_; it doesn't
87	  author design variables (that's Figma). The test is "theming the app" vs "providing
88	  design-authoring assets."
89	- **Go was declined** — no real Go UI consumer worth a target.
90

1	# Release strategy and npm organization
2	
3	This document operationalizes pantoken releases using the existing `@pantoken` npm scope,
4	Changesets, and tag-driven GitHub Actions publishing.
5	
6	Release workflow: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (package-tag driven).
7	
8	## Scope and goals
9	
10	- Keep the current `@pantoken/*` package names.
11	- Use automated semver and changelog generation.
12	- Publish via GitHub Actions on release tags.
13	- Support prerelease channels from day one.
14	
15	## npm organization model
16	
17	- Primary scope: `@pantoken`.
18	- Access: all packages published as `public`.
19	- Governance baseline:
20	  - enforce org-level 2FA for maintainers
21	  - require at least two owners
22	  - prefer trusted publishing (OIDC) from GitHub Actions
23	  - keep a break-glass token path documented and rotated
24	
25	## Versioning model
26	
27	- Tooling: Changesets (`.changeset/`).
28	- Bump model: independent package versions with internal dependency bumping set to `patch`.
29	- Changelog model:
30	  - per-package changelogs generated from changeset entries at versioning time
31	  - root `CHANGELOG.md` regenerated as an aggregate strict chronological feed (newest to oldest)
32	
33	## Release channels and tags
34	
35	Canonical package tag format: `@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z`.
36	
37	Examples:
38	
39	- `@pantoken/components@v1.0.0`
40	- `@pantoken/components@v1.1.0-beta.0`
41	
42	Release scope for a package tag:
43	
44	- target package
45	- required workspace dependents resolved from internal `workspace:*` dependency edges
46	- `@pantoken/pantoken` auto-included when the release touches its exported dependency surface
47	
48	Dist-tag mapping in CI:
49	
50	- `-alpha.N` -> `alpha`
51	- `-beta.N` -> `beta`
52	- `-rc.N` -> `rc`
53	- any other prerelease suffix -> `next`
54	- stable tags -> `latest`
55	
56	## Standard release runbook
57	
58	1. Ensure branch health.
59	2. Run gates locally:
60	   - `pnpm run ready`
61	   - `pnpm run check:publish`
62	3. Generate version and changelog updates:
63	   - `pnpm run release:version`
64	4. Regenerate aggregate root changelog:

66	
67	Bootstrap note:

71	  changelogs.
72	
73	5. Commit those updates.
74	6. Create and push one or more package tags (`@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z`).
75	7. CI computes the dependency-aware publish set and publishes with the resolved dist-tag.
76	8. Verify published versions in npm and install from a clean external project.
77

80	1. Enter prerelease mode:
81	   - `pnpm run release:pre:enter`
82	2. Create changesets for upcoming prerelease changes.

84	4. CI publishes to prerelease dist-tag.

I now have a thorough understanding. Key findings that shape the strategy:

- pantoken doesn't depend on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package at all. The security-relevant surface is **`@instructure/ui-icons` (^11.7.3, runtime dep of `@pantoken/core`)** and **eight `@instructure/ui-*` React packages (^11.7.3, used only by `renderers/react-markdown`)**. Those `^11.7.3` ranges already admit 11.7.4.
- The design-token source is a **separate, GitHub-only, unpinned** repo (`github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens`, versioned `1.0.0` — decoupled from the 11.7.x line). That unpinned ref is the reproducibility hole.
- The entire upstream blast radius is two files: `packages/core/src/build.ts` (token-tree shape) and `packages/core/src/icons.ts` (ui-icons filesystem layout). Everything else reads vendored IR from `@pantoken/tokens`.
- There's **no golden snapshot** of resolved output — drift checks today are self-containment only (`danglingReferences`/`unknownReferences`), not value-diff across upstream versions. Deprecations are authored inline per component; there's no token-level deprecation ledger. No Renovate/Dependabot. Provenance capture exists but is best-effort and unpinned.

Let me have two Plan agents design the two hardest pieces while I confirm a few forks with you.

CONTEXT (verified):
- pantoken resolves Instructure's design tokens + icons into a canonical `Token[]` IR. The ONLY upstream ingestion happens in `packages/core/src/build.ts` (`buildTokens({theme})`, reads `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens`) and `packages/core/src/icons.ts` (`collectIcons`, reads `@instructure/ui-icons` off the filesystem).
- `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` calls `buildTokens` for 3 themes (rebrand, canvas, canvasHighContrast), writes `generated/<theme>.json`, `generated/raw.json`, and `generated/meta.json` (provenance: `{upstream, upstreamVersion}`). All `generated/` is GITIGNORED (a deliberate repo convention — generated artifacts are reproduced on build).
- Token IR shape (`packages/model/src/index.ts`): `Token = {name, syntax, inherits, value, themed?, refersTo?, meta?}`. Icons are `<image>` tokens with `meta.kind==="icon"`.
- Existing drift harness: `packages/utils/src/index.ts` exports `danglingReferences(css)` (self-containment) and `unknownReferences(text, ir)` (bridge refs must be real tokens). `tools/validate-generated/index.ts` runs them across generator packages + bridges as a gate.

GOAL: a foundational, reusable mechanism so upgrading upstream (11.7.4 now, 11.7.5 / 11.8.0 later) is semi-automated: bump the pin, run one command, get a machine-readable + human-readable report that CLASSIFIES every change into buckets and SURFACES the points needing manual intervention. Buckets to design for: added tokens, removed tokens (deprecation candidates), value changes (normalization review — color/size/etc.), new dangling/unknown refs, added icons, removed/renamed icons, `@property` syntax changes.

2. The diff engine: where it lives (propose `tools/`), its function signatures, how it reads old vs new, and the classified report shape (JSON + a Markdown summary).
3. How it integrates with `vp run` tasks and CI (a new `gate:upstream`/`upgrade:check`? a report artifact on the PR?), and how it becomes semi-automated for future bumps.
4. How the tool reuses existing helpers (`resolveTokens`, `danglingReferences`, `unknownReferences`, provenance `meta.json`) rather than reinventing.

Read the files above to ground the design. Report concrete paths and signatures.

Design (do NOT implement — plan-mode research; read-only) two reusable artifacts for the pantoken monorepo (`/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken`): (1) a token-level deprecation ledger, and (2) a version-support / compatibility manifest for downstream consumers. Return a concrete design with file paths, schemas, and how they wire into existing machinery.

CONTEXT (verified):
- Deprecations TODAY exist only at the component-CSS-modifier level, authored INLINE in each component's cssdoc doc comment as `@modifier -alias — @deprecated {@link .-canonical}`, discovered by a regex in `formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts` (`DEPRECATED_ALIAS`, `deprecatedAliasPairs`, `withAliases`), which clones the canonical CSS rule under the deprecated alias name. Design how it's produced (fed by the drift diff — a companion tool is being designed separately), how a "deprecated alias" token could be emitted into the IR/CSS so consumers get a compatibility shim, and how removals surface a migration note. 3. How both integrate with the release flow (changesets) and CI so future bumps (11.7.5/11.8.0) update them semi-automatically or fail the gate when out of date.

options.description: Build the drift/diff + deprecation + compat pipeline, then use it to perform the 11.7.4 upgrade as its inaugural run — goldens, changesets, and all. One cohesive effort; the 11.7.4 diff is the proof the machinery works.

options.label: Machinery only

questions.question: How should we pin the GitHub-only `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` so upgrades are reproducible and deliberate?

options.label: Pin to a commit SHA
options.description: github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#<sha>. Fully reproducible; upgrades become an explicit SHA bump that flows through the drift pipeline. Requires manually choosing the SHA each bump (that's the intended control point).

options.label: Pin to an upstream tag
options.description: Pin to a release tag/branch if upstream publishes them. Cleaner than a SHA but only works if the repo tags releases — I'd verify that first.

options.label: Full resolved IR goldens
options.description: Commit the full per-theme resolved IR JSON as golden files. Exact and complete, but large, noisy PR diffs and a bigger break from the gitignore convention.

options.label: Compare against published npm
options.description: No committed baseline; CI diffs the new build against the last-published @pantoken/tokens artifact. Keeps gitignore intact, but drift isn't visible in the PR diff and depends on npm availability.

questions.question: How formal should the consumer version-support / compatibility layer be?

options.label: Manifest + generated doc table
options.description: A machine-readable compatibility.json (upstream version/range ↔ pantoken version ↔ validated consumers: WordPress, Angular, Vitepress, wrappers), validated in CI, rendered into a human doc table. Reusable and enforceable.

options.label: Hand-maintained doc table
options.description: A Markdown table in docs/internal you update by hand each release. Low effort, no enforcement, drifts easily.

options.label: Per-package compat field
options.description: A pantoken.compat field in each consumer's package.json, aggregated at build. Colocated with each consumer, but scattered and harder to read as one matrix.

# Design: token deprecation ledger + compatibility manifest

## Grounding summary (what exists today)

- Vendored IR is written by `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` → `formats/tokens/generated/{rebrand,canvas,canvasHighContrast}.json` + `raw.json` + `meta.json` (`{upstream, upstreamVersion}`). `@pantoken/tokens` (`formats/tokens/src/index.ts`) just imports those JSON files and re-exports arrays. Exports are `"."` and `"./raw"` only; `meta.json` is not currently exported.
- `buildTokens` (`packages/core/src/build.ts`) runs plugin `tokens` hooks as its last step (step 6), and `defineToken` (`packages/core/src/plugin.ts:54`) auto-derives `syntax: "*"` + `refersTo` for a single `var(--instui-*)` value.
- `toCss` (`formats/css/src/to-css.ts:71`) routes any contextual token (a `var()`/`light-dark()` value) into the `:root` declarations block; concrete tokens become `@property`. So a `var()` forwarder token becomes a real CSS shim in every downstream format for free.
- Drift primitives live in `@pantoken/utils` (`packages/utils/src/index.ts`): `tokenNames`, `unknownReferences`, `danglingReferences`. `tools/validate-generated/index.ts` is the drift gate; its `GENERATOR_PKGS`, `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS`, `BRIDGES`, `SELF_CONTAINED` arrays already enumerate exactly which consumers are validated and by which check.
- Release uses a writer/gate pair convention: `sync:repository` writes, `gate:repository` verifies (`vite.config.ts:116-123`). `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset whenever a publishable package's shipped source changes — regenerating `generated/*.json` counts.
- The inline-alias philosophy in `formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts` clones a canonical rule body under the alias name. At the token layer we can do better than a body-copy: a `var()` forwarder keeps theming/`light-dark()` flowing through automatically.

---

## Artifact 1 — token deprecation ledger

### File

`formats/tokens/deprecations.json` — committed, hand-authored (package root, beside `generated/`, not inside it since `generated/` is machine-written). It's the durable, reviewed policy record; the companion drift diff only *proposes* entries.

### Schema

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./deprecations.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "token": "--instui-color-background-brand-old", // removed/renamed upstream token
      "since": "1.0.0",                    // upstream version it disappeared in (== meta.upstreamVersion)
      "policy": "alias",                   // "alias" | "removed"
      "replacement": "--instui-color-background-brand",
      "note": "Renamed upstream; forwards to the canonical brand background."
    },
    {
      "token": "--instui-legacy-spacing-xxs",
      "since": "1.0.0",
      "policy": "removed",
      "replacement": "--instui-spacing-xx-small", // migration target only; no shim emitted
      "note": "Hard-removed upstream. Migrate to the canonical spacing token."
    }
  ]
}
```

Policy semantics, reusing the inline-alias philosophy at the token layer:
- `"alias"` → emit a compatibility-shim token into the IR: `define({ name: token, value: "var(<replacement>)", meta: { deprecated: {...} } })`. `defineToken` yields `syntax:"*"`, `refersTo: replacement`; `toCss` emits it as a `:root` declaration, so css/scss/less/stylus/wordpress/vanilla all get the shim automatically. This is the token analog of `withAliases`, but via `var()` forwarding (theming flows through) instead of a body clone.
- `"removed"` → **not** emitted. Surfaces only as a migration note (docs + CHANGELOG). Any pantoken-authored output still referencing it is already caught by `unknownReferences` in `validate-generated`.

### `@pantoken/model` type additions (`packages/model/src/index.ts`)

Zero-dependency, types only — fits the package's role as the IR contract:

```ts
/** Policy for an upstream token that was removed or renamed. */
export type DeprecationPolicy = "alias" | "removed";

/** One entry in the token deprecation ledger. */
export interface DeprecationEntry {
  token: string;
  since: string;
  policy: DeprecationPolicy;
  replacement?: string;   // required for "alias"
  note?: string;
}

/** The committed ledger shape (formats/tokens/deprecations.json). */
export interface DeprecationLedger {
  version: number;
  entries: DeprecationEntry[];
}
```

And one field on the existing `TokenMeta` (line 29-43) so a shim token carries its provenance into the IR (visible to consumers, docs, and the gate):

```ts
/** Present on an emitted compatibility-shim token (policy "alias"). */
deprecated?: { replacement?: string; since?: string; note?: string };
```

### Production / wiring

- New plugin `plugins/pantoken/deprecations` exporting `deprecationShims(ledger: DeprecationLedger): PantokenPlugin`. Its `tokens` hook appends one forwarder per `alias` entry:

  ```ts
  tokens: ({ tokens, define }) => [
    ...tokens,
    ...ledger.entries
      .filter((e) => e.policy === "alias" && e.replacement)
      .map((e) => define({
        name: e.token,
        value: `var(${e.replacement})`,
        meta: { deprecated: { replacement: e.replacement, since: e.since, note: e.note } },
      })),
  ]
  ```

- Insert it in `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` so shims bake into the vendored JSON everyone reads: `buildTokens({ theme, plugins: [deprecationShims(ledger)] })`. No separate release wiring is then needed — shims ship with `@pantoken/tokens` and every downstream format.
- **Fed by the drift diff** (companion tool): it compares `tokenNames(previousIR)` vs `tokenNames(newIR)` after an upstream bump; disappeared names become candidate entries pre-filled with `since = new meta.upstreamVersion`. A human sets `policy` + `replacement`. New gate `gate:token-drift` fails if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed) — this is the forcing function.
- Optionally export the ledger from `@pantoken/tokens` (`"./deprecations"`) so tooling/docs can read it without a file path.

---

## Artifact 2 — compatibility manifest

### File

`compatibility.json` at repo root (a repo-wide release fact, like a lockfile-adjacent manifest), rendered into a human page at `docs/compatibility.md`. It's a writer/gate pair, mirroring `sync:repository`/`gate:repository`.

### Schema

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./compatibility.schema.json",
  "generatedAt": "2026-07-24",
  "upstream": {
    // token source — governs the token IR; unpinned github, provenance from meta.json
    "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens": {
      "range": "github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens",
      "resolved": "1.0.0",
      "feeds": "token-ir"
    },
    // icon source — governs the icon layer
    "@instructure/ui-icons": { "range": "^11.7.3", "resolved": "11.7.4", "feeds": "icons" },
    // the eight ui-* React packages — govern renderers/react-markdown ONLY
    "@instructure/ui-view":  { "range": "^11.7.3", "resolved": "11.7.4", "feeds": "react-markdown" }
    // ...ui-heading, ui-text, ui-link, ui-list, ui-table, ui-img, ui-alerts
  },
  "consumers": {
    "platforms/wordpress":       { "package": "@pantoken/wordpress",  "validatedBy": ["generated", "reference-integrity"] },
    "renderers/angular":         { "package": "@pantoken/angular",    "validatedBy": ["finalized-css"] },
    "renderers/vitepress":       { "package": "@pantoken/vitepress",  "validatedBy": ["generated", "reference-integrity", "finalized-css"] },
    "renderers/react-markdown":  { "package": "@pantoken/react-markdown", "instui": "^11.7.3" }
  }
}
```

The two-tier `upstream` split matters: the github-only design-tokens line (unpinned, "1.0.0") feeds the token IR, while the `^11.7.x` ui-* line feeds only `renderers/react-markdown`. The manifest records which pantoken layer each upstream governs so an 11.7.5/11.8.0 bump maps to the right blast radius.

### Generation + validation

- `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` (writer). Sources:
  - token-source `resolved` ← `formats/tokens/generated/meta.json`.
  - each ui-* `resolved` ← installed `node_modules/.../package.json` via `require.resolve` (same technique `generate.ts:31` already uses for provenance).
  - each `range` ← the `catalog` block in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
  - `consumers` + `validatedBy` ← derived from `validate-generated`'s `GENERATOR_PKGS` / `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS` / `BRIDGES` arrays (export them as a shared constant so the manifest and the gate can't drift from each other).
- `scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts` (gate). Regenerates the expected manifest in memory and diffs against committed `compatibility.json`; fails if stale. Also asserts `meta.upstreamVersion === upstream["@instructure/instructure-design-tokens"].resolved`.
- Human render: a small doc generator turns `compatibility.json` into a support-matrix table in `docs/compatibility.md`, built inside the existing docs VitePress pipeline.

---

## Artifact 3 — release-flow & CI integration

New tasks in `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks`, following the existing DAG conventions (everything needing generated output `dependsOn: ["build:all"]`):

```jsonc
"sync:compatibility":  { "command": "node scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts", "dependsOn": ["build:all"] },
"gate:compatibility":  { "command": "node scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts",     "dependsOn": ["build:all"] },
"gate:token-drift":    { "command": "node tools/token-drift/index.ts --check",          "dependsOn": ["build:all"] }
```

Add `gate:compatibility` and `gate:token-drift` to the `ready:all` fan-out (and/or `gate:publish`).

How a future bump behaves:
- Bumping the catalog (11.7.5 / 11.8.0, or a design-tokens github bump) regenerates `generated/*.json` + `meta.json`. That's shipped-source churn in `@pantoken/tokens`, so `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset — no new wiring needed there.
- The same PR must also: (a) update `compatibility.json` or `gate:compatibility` fails, and (b) add `deprecations.json` entries for any disappeared token or `gate:token-drift` fails.
- `alias` shims need no extra release step — they're baked into the vendored IR at generate time and flow through every format. A changeset note ("adds compatibility shim for `--instui-…`") documents them; `removed` entries render as migration notes in `docs/compatibility.md` / the tokens CHANGELOG.

### Notable design choices / trade-offs

- Token-layer aliases use `var()` forwarding (`refersTo`) rather than the component-layer body-clone in `withAliases`, so shims inherit theming and `light-dark()` automatically. Worth calling out as a deliberate divergence from the inline philosophy.
- Baking shims into the vendored JSON (vs. emitting them live in each consumer's `toCss` call) keeps `@pantoken/tokens` the single source of truth and lets `validate-generated` see shim tokens as *defined* (so bridges referencing them don't trip `unknownReferences`).
- `deprecations.json` and `compatibility.json` deliberately live in different scopes: the ledger is package-local to `@pantoken/tokens` (it annotates that package's IR), while the manifest is repo-wide (it spans all consumers + two upstream tiers).

### Critical files for implementation

- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` (bake alias shims + write meta; ledger read point)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/model/src/index.ts` (add `DeprecationEntry`/`DeprecationLedger`, `TokenMeta.deprecated`)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/tools/validate-generated/index.ts` (export consumer arrays; drift-gate integration)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/vite.config.ts` (new `sync:/gate:compatibility`, `gate:token-drift` tasks in the DAG)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/scripts/release/check-changeset-coverage.ts` (confirms bump PRs stay covered; pattern reference for the new writer/gate scripts)

# Instructure UI upgrade strategy — a reusable, semi-automated pipeline (first run: 11.7.4 / design-tokens v1.5.0)

## Context

`@instructure/ui@11.7.4` shipped security fixes, so we need to update. But a bump also pulls in
token, color, size, deprecation, and icon changes, and today pantoken has no repeatable way to see
what changed or to force the manual-review points to the surface. This plan builds a **foundational,
reusable upgrade pipeline** — drift detection, a token deprecation ledger, and a consumer
compatibility manifest — then **runs it to perform the 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade as its first pass**.
After this, 11.7.5 and 11.8.0 become: bump the pin, run one command, review a classified report, and
either accept or intervene. The same manifest lets us mark version support for consumers (WordPress,
Angular, Vitepress, and the framework wrappers).

## Verified current state (grounds every decision below)

- **pantoken never depends on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package.** The upstream surface is exactly
  three tiers:
  - `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` — GitHub-only, feeds the **token IR**. Consumed only in
    `packages/core/src/build.ts`. Currently `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens` with **no
    ref** (floating); the lockfile happens to sit on commit `0db8a86…` = **tag `v1.4.0`**. Latest is
    **`v1.5.0`** (`ae8f600…`).
  - `@instructure/ui-icons` — `^11.7.3`, feeds the **icon layer**. Consumed only in
    `packages/core/src/icons.ts` (reads the package off the filesystem).
  - Eight `@instructure/ui-*` React packages (`ui-heading`, `-text`, `-link`, `-list`, `-table`,
    `-view`, `-img`, `-alerts`) — `^11.7.3`, consumed **only by `renderers/react-markdown`**.
- All pins live in the `catalog:` block of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Everything downstream reads the
  vendored IR from `@pantoken/tokens` (`formats/tokens/generated/*.json`), never `@pantoken/core`.
- **Provenance is broken.** `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` records `upstreamVersion` by reading
  the upstream `package.json.version`, which is **stuck at `1.0.0` on `main` across every tag**. So
  `meta.json` says `1.0.0` while we're really on `v1.4.0`. Provenance must record the **pinned tag +
  resolved commit**, not `package.json.version`.
- **No golden/value baseline exists.** Drift checks today are self-containment only —
  `danglingReferences` / `unknownReferences` in `packages/utils/src/index.ts`, run by
  `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`. Nothing captures resolved token values to diff across upstream
  versions.
- **Deprecations exist only at the component-CSS-modifier level**, authored inline as
  `@modifier -alias — @deprecated {@link .-canonical}` and cloned by `formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts`.
  There is no token-level deprecation record.
- The task DAG is `run.tasks` in `vite.config.ts`; gates funnel through `ready:all` and `gate:publish`.
  `scripts/release/check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when a publishable
  package's shipped source changes (re-vendoring `generated/*.json` counts). CI is
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No Renovate/Dependabot.

## Locked decisions (from you)

1. **Build the machinery, then run it to perform the 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade** as the inaugural pass.
2. **Pin the GitHub-only design-tokens to a tag** — verified viable (`v1.0.0`–`v1.5.0` exist; GitHub
   Releases from `v1.3.0`). Move to `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#v1.5.0`.
3. **Compact committed token manifest** as the diff baseline (not full IR goldens, not npm-only).
4. **Machine-readable `compatibility.json` + generated doc table**, validated in CI.

## What we build

Everything reuses existing helpers (`resolveTokens`/`makeResolver`, `danglingReferences`,
`unknownReferences`, the provenance capture, the `validate-generated` package lists) rather than
reinventing. All new tasks follow the `dependsOn: ["build:all"]` convention so codegen runs once.

### A. Fix provenance + pin the token source

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog: change the design-tokens entry to
  `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#v1.5.0`; bump `@instructure/ui-icons` and the eight
  `@instructure/ui-*` packages `^11.7.3` → `^11.7.4`.
- `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`: rewrite the provenance block to record
  `{ designTokens: { ref, commit }, uiIcons: { resolved } }` — read the design-tokens **ref from the
  catalog pin** and the **commit from `pnpm-lock.yaml`** (the tarball URL carries the sha); read
  `uiIcons` via the existing `require.resolve(... /package.json)` trick. Keep `package.json.version`
  only as an untrusted secondary field. Export `meta.json` from `@pantoken/tokens` (`"./meta"`) so
  tooling and docs can read provenance without a file path.

### B. Upstream-drift tool — the core of the pipeline

New private package **`tools/upstream-diff`** (`@pantoken/upstream-diff`), mirroring the layout and
task wiring of `tools/validate-generated`.

- **Baseline** (committed, compact, deliberate exception to the `generated/` gitignore):
  `tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json`. Per theme: `name → { syntax, inherits, value,
  resolved, themed?, refersTo? }`; icons: `name → { source, style, viewBox, bidirectional, svgHash }`
  (hash the fat data-URI, don't store it). Plus the `provenance` block from (A).
- **Library** `tools/upstream-diff/src/index.ts` (pure, unit-tested):
  - `buildManifest({ themes, provenance })` — projects the built IR; uses `resolveTokens` at
    `mode: "light"` and `"dark"` for the `resolved` field so a change deep in the primitive chain
    surfaces at the semantic layer, and `light-dark()` branch / `themed` flips are caught.
  - `diffManifests(before, after): UpstreamDiff` — classifies **per theme** into buckets that map
    1:1 to your requirements: `addedTokens`, `removedTokens` (deprecation candidates),
    `valueChanges` (with a `category` of `color | length | number | image | other` from `syntax`, to
    route the color/size normalization review), `syntaxChanges` (`@property` registration changes),
    `refChanges`, `addedIcons`, `removedIcons`/renames (a removed name whose `svgHash` matches an added
    name is reported once as a rename), `changedIcons`. Plus `danglingDelta` / `unknownDelta` (new
    reference breakage the bump introduced) and a `manualReview` subset.
  - `toJsonReport(diff)` and `toMarkdownReport(diff)`.
- **Runner** `tools/upstream-diff/index.ts` — imports `themes` from `@pantoken/tokens` and provenance
  from `@pantoken/tokens/meta`, builds the current manifest, diffs against the committed baseline,
  writes the JSON + Markdown report to a gitignored `report/` dir, prints the Markdown, and **exits
  non-zero when drift exists but the baseline wasn't updated in the same change**. A `--bless` mode
  rewrites `baseline/manifest.json` from the current build (maintainer action, never the gate).
- **Reuse, don't duplicate:** extract `validate-generated`'s `SELF_CONTAINED` / `BRIDGES` /
  `GENERATOR_PKGS` / `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS` arrays into a shared const both tools import, so drift
  attribution and the existing gate can't fall out of sync.

### C. Token deprecation ledger — "updated deprecation set" + "removing deprecated elements"

- **`formats/tokens/deprecations.json`** (committed, hand-authored policy; the diff only *proposes*
  entries). Each entry: `{ token, since, policy: "alias" | "removed", replacement?, note? }`.
- **`packages/model/src/index.ts`**: add zero-dep types `DeprecationPolicy`, `DeprecationEntry`,
  `DeprecationLedger`, and a `deprecated?: { replacement?, since?, note? }` field on `TokenMeta`.
- **`plugins/pantoken/deprecations`** exporting `deprecationShims(ledger)`: a `PantokenPlugin` whose
  `tokens` hook appends one **`var()` forwarder** per `alias` entry (`value: "var(<replacement>)"`).
  `defineToken` derives `refersTo`, and `toCss` emits it as a `:root` declaration — so the shim flows
  into css/scss/less/stylus/wordpress/vanilla for free, and inherits theming/`light-dark()`
  automatically (a deliberate improvement over the component-layer body-clone). Wire it into
  `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` so shims bake into the vendored JSON everyone reads.
- `"removed"` entries emit nothing — they render as migration notes in docs + the tokens CHANGELOG.
- **Deprecation lifecycle:** a shim is added at the bump that removed the upstream token, kept through
  the current minor line, and pruned at the next major. Reconcile the existing inline **component**
  aliases the same way during this pass — that's the "removing deprecated elements" step.
- **Forcing function:** the upstream-diff `removedTokens` bucket feeds `gate:token-drift`, which fails
  if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed).

### D. Consumer compatibility manifest — "marking version support"

- **`compatibility.json`** at repo root, with a two-tier `upstream` block (design-tokens → token-ir;
  ui-icons → icons; the eight ui-* → react-markdown), each carrying `{ range, resolved, feeds }`, and
  a `consumers` block (`platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`,
  `renderers/react-markdown`, plus the framework wrappers) with the `validatedBy` checks each already
  passes.
- **Writer/gate pair** (mirrors `sync:repository` / `gate:repository`):
  `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` sources `resolved` from provenance + installed
  `package.json`s, `range` from the catalog, and `consumers`/`validatedBy` from the shared
  `validate-generated` arrays. `scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts` regenerates in memory and
  fails if the committed file is stale (and asserts provenance agrees).
- Render `compatibility.json` into a support-matrix table at `docs/compatibility.md` inside the
  existing VitePress/TypeDoc docs build.

### E. CI + task wiring

- `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks`: add `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless`
  (`@pantoken/upstream-diff#diff|bless`), `sync:compatibility` / `gate:compatibility`, and
  `gate:token-drift`. Root `package.json`: matching `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless` scripts.
- Add `gate:compatibility` and `gate:token-drift` to `ready:all` (and `gate:publish`). **Do not** add
  the full `upgrade:check` diff to `ready:all` — it would fail every intentional bump until blessed
  and cost a diff on unrelated PRs.
- New CI job **`upstream-drift`** in `ci.yml`, gated by a `paths-filter` on `pnpm-workspace.yaml` +
  `pnpm-lock.yaml` (same pattern as the existing docs job): restore the vp cache, build, run
  `upgrade:check`, upload the report artifact, post/update a sticky PR comment with the Markdown
  summary, and fail if drift is unblessed in the PR. This is the lockfile-style invariant that keeps
  the committed baseline honest.
- Existing `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when `generated/*.json` churns —
  no new wiring needed there.

### F. Execute the inaugural 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade

1. Apply the pin edits from (A); `vp install`.
2. `vp run -r build` to re-vendor; `vp run upgrade:check` to produce the first report.
3. **Bootstrap the baseline** by blessing the *pre-bump* state first if needed (build at the old pin,
   `--bless`), so the first real diff is meaningful — otherwise the first run just records v1.5.0 as
   the baseline with nothing to compare. (Decide during implementation: bless at `v1.4.0` then diff to
   `v1.5.0`, giving a true first drift report.)
4. Work the report: author `deprecations.json` entries for `removedTokens`; review `valueChanges`
   (color/size) against the normalization code (`build.ts` light-dark collapse, `color.ts` `applyModify`,
   `utils.ts` `cssSyntaxForValue`); confirm `addedTokens` land in the IR; resolve any
   `danglingDelta`/`unknownDelta`.
5. `vp run upgrade:bless` to commit the v1.5.0 baseline; `vp run sync:compatibility` to write
   `compatibility.json`; regenerate `docs/compatibility.md`.
6. Verify `renderers/react-markdown` still builds/tests against the ui-* `^11.7.4` bump.
7. Add changesets; run the full gate (below).

## Critical files

- Pins/provenance: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`, `formats/tokens/src/index.ts` (add `./meta` export).
- Drift tool (new): `tools/upstream-diff/{src/index.ts, index.ts, baseline/manifest.json, package.json}`; shared lists refactored out of `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`.
- Deprecations: `formats/tokens/deprecations.json` (new), `packages/model/src/index.ts`, `plugins/pantoken/deprecations/` (new plugin), `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` (wire the plugin).
- Compatibility: `compatibility.json` (new), `scripts/release/{generate,check}-compatibility.ts` (new), `docs/compatibility.md` (generated).
- Wiring: `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Reusability — the future-bump runbook (11.7.5, 11.8.0)

# Instructure UI upgrade strategy — a reusable, semi-automated pipeline (first run: 11.7.4 / design-tokens v1.5.0)

## Context

`@instructure/ui@11.7.4` shipped security fixes, so we need to update. But a bump also pulls in
token, color, size, deprecation, and icon changes, and today pantoken has no repeatable way to see
what changed or to force the manual-review points to the surface. This plan builds a **foundational,
reusable upgrade pipeline** — drift detection, a token deprecation ledger, and a consumer
compatibility manifest — then **runs it to perform the 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade as its first pass**.
After this, 11.7.5 and 11.8.0 become: bump the pin, run one command, review a classified report, and
either accept or intervene. The same manifest lets us mark version support for consumers (WordPress,
Angular, Vitepress, and the framework wrappers).

## Verified current state (grounds every decision below)

- **pantoken never depends on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package.** The upstream surface is exactly
  three tiers:
  - `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` — GitHub-only, feeds the **token IR**. Consumed only in
    `packages/core/src/build.ts`. Currently `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens` with **no
    ref** (floating); the lockfile happens to sit on commit `0db8a86…` = **tag `v1.4.0`**. Latest is
    **`v1.5.0`** (`ae8f600…`).
  - `@instructure/ui-icons` — `^11.7.3`, feeds the **icon layer**. Consumed only in
    `packages/core/src/icons.ts` (reads the package off the filesystem).
  - Eight `@instructure/ui-*` React packages (`ui-heading`, `-text`, `-link`, `-list`, `-table`,
    `-view`, `-img`, `-alerts`) — `^11.7.3`, consumed **only by `renderers/react-markdown`**.
- All pins live in the `catalog:` block of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Everything downstream reads the
  vendored IR from `@pantoken/tokens` (`formats/tokens/generated/*.json`), never `@pantoken/core`.
- **Provenance is broken.** `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` records `upstreamVersion` by reading
  the upstream `package.json.version`, which is **stuck at `1.0.0` on `main` across every tag**. So
  `meta.json` says `1.0.0` while we're really on `v1.4.0`. Provenance must record the **pinned tag +
  resolved commit**, not `package.json.version`.
- **No golden/value baseline exists.** Drift checks today are self-containment only —
  `danglingReferences` / `unknownReferences` in `packages/utils/src/index.ts`, run by
  `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`. Nothing captures resolved token values to diff across upstream
  versions.
- **Deprecations exist only at the component-CSS-modifier level**, authored inline as
  `@modifier -alias — @deprecated {@link .-canonical}` and cloned by `formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts`.
  There is no token-level deprecation record.
- The task DAG is `run.tasks` in `vite.config.ts`; gates funnel through `ready:all` and `gate:publish`.
  `scripts/release/check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when a publishable
  package's shipped source changes (re-vendoring `generated/*.json` counts). CI is
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No Renovate/Dependabot.

## Locked decisions (from you)

1. **Build the machinery, then run it to perform the 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade** as the inaugural pass.
2. **Pin the GitHub-only design-tokens to a tag** — verified viable (`v1.0.0`–`v1.5.0` exist; GitHub
   Releases from `v1.3.0`). Move to `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#v1.5.0`.
3. **Compact committed token manifest** as the diff baseline (not full IR goldens, not npm-only).
4. **Machine-readable `compatibility.json` + generated doc table**, validated in CI.

## What we build

Everything reuses existing helpers (`resolveTokens`/`makeResolver`, `danglingReferences`,
`unknownReferences`, the provenance capture, the `validate-generated` package lists) rather than
reinventing. All new tasks follow the `dependsOn: ["build:all"]` convention so codegen runs once.

### A. Fix provenance + pin the token source

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog: change the design-tokens entry to
  `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#v1.5.0`; bump `@instructure/ui-icons` and the eight
  `@instructure/ui-*` packages `^11.7.3` → `^11.7.4`.
- `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`: rewrite the provenance block to record
  `{ designTokens: { ref, commit }, uiIcons: { resolved } }` — read the design-tokens **ref from the
  catalog pin** and the **commit from `pnpm-lock.yaml`** (the tarball URL carries the sha); read
  `uiIcons` via the existing `require.resolve(... /package.json)` trick. Keep `package.json.version`
  only as an untrusted secondary field. Export `meta.json` from `@pantoken/tokens` (`"./meta"`) so
  tooling and docs can read provenance without a file path.

### B. Upstream-drift tool — the core of the pipeline

New private package **`tools/upstream-diff`** (`@pantoken/upstream-diff`), mirroring the layout and
task wiring of `tools/validate-generated`.

- **Baseline** (committed, compact, deliberate exception to the `generated/` gitignore):
  `tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json`. Per theme: `name → { syntax, inherits, value,
  resolved, themed?, refersTo? }`; icons: `name → { source, style, viewBox, bidirectional, svgHash }`
  (hash the fat data-URI, don't store it). Plus the `provenance` block from (A).
- **Library** `tools/upstream-diff/src/index.ts` (pure, unit-tested):
  - `buildManifest({ themes, provenance })` — projects the built IR; uses `resolveTokens` at
    `mode: "light"` and `"dark"` for the `resolved` field so a change deep in the primitive chain
    surfaces at the semantic layer, and `light-dark()` branch / `themed` flips are caught.
  - `diffManifests(before, after): UpstreamDiff` — classifies **per theme** into buckets that map
    1:1 to your requirements: `addedTokens`, `removedTokens` (deprecation candidates),
    `valueChanges` (with a `category` of `color | length | number | image | other` from `syntax`, to
    route the color/size normalization review), `syntaxChanges` (`@property` registration changes),
    `refChanges`, `addedIcons`, `removedIcons`/renames (a removed name whose `svgHash` matches an added
    name is reported once as a rename), `changedIcons`. Plus `danglingDelta` / `unknownDelta` (new
    reference breakage the bump introduced) and a `manualReview` subset.

  rewrites `baseline/manifest.json` from the current build (maintainer action, never the gate).

- **`formats/tokens/deprecations.json`** (committed, hand-authored policy; the diff only *proposes*
  entries). Each entry: `{ token, since, policy: "alias" | "removed", replacement?, note? }`.
- **`packages/model/src/index.ts`**: add zero-dep types `DeprecationPolicy`, `DeprecationEntry`,
  `DeprecationLedger`, and a `deprecated?: { replacement?, since?, note? }` field on `TokenMeta`.
- **`plugins/pantoken/deprecations`** exporting `deprecationShims(ledger)`: a `PantokenPlugin` whose
  `tokens` hook appends one **`var()` forwarder** per `alias` entry (`value: "var(<replacement>)"`).
  `defineToken` derives `refersTo`, and `toCss` emits it as a `:root` declaration — so the shim flows
  into css/scss/less/stylus/wordpress/vanilla for free, and inherits theming/`light-dark()`
  automatically (a deliberate improvement over the component-layer body-clone). Wire it into
  `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` so shims bake into the vendored JSON everyone reads.
- `"removed"` entries emit nothing — they render as migration notes in docs + the tokens CHANGELOG.
- **Deprecation lifecycle:** a shim is added at the bump that removed the upstream token, kept through
  the current minor line, and pruned at the next major. Reconcile the existing inline **component**
  aliases the same way during this pass — that's the "removing deprecated elements" step.
- **Forcing function:** the upstream-diff `removedTokens` bucket feeds `gate:token-drift`, which fails
  if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed).

### D. Consumer compatibility manifest — "marking version support"

- **`compatibility.json`** at repo root, with a two-tier `upstream` block (design-tokens → token-ir;
  ui-icons → icons; the eight ui-* → react-markdown), each carrying `{ range, resolved, feeds }`, and
  a `consumers` block (`platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`,
  `renderers/react-markdown`, plus the framework wrappers) with the `validatedBy` checks each already
  passes.
- **Writer/gate pair** (mirrors `sync:repository` / `gate:repository`):
  `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` sources `resolved` from provenance + installed
  `package.json`s, `range` from the catalog, and `consumers`/`validatedBy` from the shared
  `validate-generated` arrays. `scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts` regenerates in memory and
  fails if the committed file is stale (and asserts provenance agrees).
- Render `compatibility.json` into a support-matrix table at `docs/compatibility.md` inside the
  existing VitePress/TypeDoc docs build.

- `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks`: add `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless`

  summary, and fail if drift is unblessed in the PR. This is the lockfile-style invariant that keeps
  the committed baseline honest.
- Existing `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when `generated/*.json` churns —
  no new wiring needed there.

7. Add changesets; run the full gate (below).

- Drift tool (new): `tools/upstream-diff/{src/index.ts, index.ts, baseline/manifest.json, package.json}`; shared lists refactored out of `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`.

    1:1 to your requirements: `addedTokens`, `removedTokens` (deprecation candidates),
    `valueChanges` (with a `category` of `color | length | number | image | other` from `syntax`, to
    route the color/size normalization review), `syntaxChanges` (`@property` registration changes),
    `refChanges`, `addedIcons`, `removedIcons`/renames (a removed name whose `svgHash` matches an added
    name is reported once as a rename), `changedIcons`. Plus `danglingDelta` / `unknownDelta` (new
    reference breakage the bump introduced) and a `manualReview` subset.
  - `toJsonReport(diff)` and `toMarkdownReport(diff)`.
- **Runner** `tools/upstream-diff/index.ts` — imports `themes` from `@pantoken/tokens` and provenance
  from `@pantoken/tokens/meta`, builds the current manifest, diffs against the committed baseline,
  writes the JSON + Markdown report to a gitignored `report/` dir, prints the Markdown, and **exits
  non-zero when drift exists but the baseline wasn't updated in the same change**. A `--bless` mode
  rewrites `baseline/manifest.json` from the current build (maintainer action, never the gate).
- **Reuse, don't duplicate:** extract `validate-generated`'s `SELF_CONTAINED` / `BRIDGES` /
  `GENERATOR_PKGS` / `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS` arrays into a shared const both tools import, so drift
  attribution and the existing gate can't fall out of sync.

### C. Token deprecation ledger — "updated deprecation set" + "removing deprecated elements"

- **`formats/tokens/deprecations.json`** (committed, hand-authored policy; the diff only *proposes*
  entries). Each entry: `{ token, since, policy: "alias" | "removed", replacement?, note? }`.
- **`packages/model/src/index.ts`**: add zero-dep types `DeprecationPolicy`, `DeprecationEntry`,
  `DeprecationLedger`, and a `deprecated?: { replacement?, since?, note? }` field on `TokenMeta`.
- **`plugins/pantoken/deprecations`** exporting `deprecationShims(ledger)`: a `PantokenPlugin` whose
  `tokens` hook appends one **`var()` forwarder** per `alias` entry (`value: "var(<replacement>)"`).
  `defineToken` derives `refersTo`, and `toCss` emits it as a `:root` declaration — so the shim flows
  into css/scss/less/stylus/wordpress/vanilla for free, and inherits theming/`light-dark()`
  automatically (a deliberate improvement over the component-layer body-clone). Wire it into
  `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` so shims bake into the vendored JSON everyone reads.
- `"removed"` entries emit nothing — they render as migration notes in docs + the tokens CHANGELOG.
- **Deprecation lifecycle:** a shim is added at the bump that removed the upstream token, kept through
  the current minor line, and pruned at the next major. Reconcile the existing inline **component**
  aliases the same way during this pass — that's the "removing deprecated elements" step.
- **Forcing function:** the upstream-diff `removedTokens` bucket feeds `gate:token-drift`, which fails
  if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed).

### D. Consumer compatibility manifest — "marking version support"

- **`compatibility.json`** at repo root, with a two-tier `upstream` block (design-tokens → token-ir;
  ui-icons → icons; the eight ui-* → react-markdown), each carrying `{ range, resolved, feeds }`, and
  a `consumers` block (`platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`,
  `renderers/react-markdown`, plus the framework wrappers) with the `validatedBy` checks each already
  passes.
- **Writer/gate pair** (mirrors `sync:repository` / `gate:repository`):
  `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` sources `resolved` from provenance + installed
  `package.json`s, `range` from the catalog, and `consumers`/`validatedBy` from the shared
  `validate-generated` arrays. `scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts` regenerates in memory and
  fails if the committed file is stale (and asserts provenance agrees).
- Render `compatibility.json` into a support-matrix table at `docs/compatibility.md` inside the
  existing VitePress/TypeDoc docs build.

### E. CI + task wiring

- `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks`: add `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless`
  (`@pantoken/upstream-diff#diff|bless`), `sync:compatibility` / `gate:compatibility`, and
  `gate:token-drift`. Root `package.json`: matching `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless` scripts.
- Add `gate:compatibility` and `gate:token-drift` to `ready:all` (and `gate:publish`). **Do not** add
  the full `upgrade:check` diff to `ready:all` — it would fail every intentional bump until blessed
  and cost a diff on unrelated PRs.
- New CI job **`upstream-drift`** in `ci.yml`, gated by a `paths-filter` on `pnpm-workspace.yaml` +
  `pnpm-lock.yaml` (same pattern as the existing docs job): restore the vp cache, build, run
  `upgrade:check`, upload the report artifact, post/update a sticky PR comment with the Markdown
  summary, and fail if drift is unblessed in the PR. This is the lockfile-style invariant that keeps
  the committed baseline honest.
- Existing `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when `generated/*.json` churns —
  no new wiring needed there.

### F. Execute the inaugural 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade

1. Apply the pin edits from (A); `vp install`.
2. `vp run -r build` to re-vendor; `vp run upgrade:check` to produce the first report.
3. **Bootstrap the baseline** by blessing the *pre-bump* state first if needed (build at the old pin,
   `--bless`), so the first real diff is meaningful — otherwise the first run just records v1.5.0 as
   the baseline with nothing to compare. (Decide during implementation: bless at `v1.4.0` then diff to
   `v1.5.0`, giving a true first drift report.)
4. Work the report: author `deprecations.json` entries for `removedTokens`; review `valueChanges`
   (color/size) against the normalization code (`build.ts` light-dark collapse, `color.ts` `applyModify`,
   `utils.ts` `cssSyntaxForValue`); confirm `addedTokens` land in the IR; resolve any
   `danglingDelta`/`unknownDelta`.
5. `vp run upgrade:bless` to commit the v1.5.0 baseline; `vp run sync:compatibility` to write
   `compatibility.json`; regenerate `docs/compatibility.md`.
6. Verify `renderers/react-markdown` still builds/tests against the ui-* `^11.7.4` bump.
7. Add changesets; run the full gate (below).

## Critical files

- Pins/provenance: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`, `formats/tokens/src/index.ts` (add `./meta` export).
- Drift tool (new): `tools/upstream-diff/{src/index.ts, index.ts, baseline/manifest.json, package.json}`; shared lists refactored out of `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`.
- Deprecations: `formats/tokens/deprecations.json` (new), `packages/model/src/index.ts`, `plugins/pantoken/deprecations/` (new plugin), `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` (wire the plugin).
- Compatibility: `compatibility.json` (new), `scripts/release/{generate,check}-compatibility.ts` (new), `docs/compatibility.md` (generated).
- Wiring: `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Reusability — the future-bump runbook (11.7.5, 11.8.0)

1. Bump the catalog pin (a new tag for design-tokens, or `^11.7.x` for the ui-* line); `vp install`.
2. `vp run upgrade:check` → read the classified Markdown report; act on `manualReview`.
3. Author `deprecations.json` entries for removed tokens (or the gate blocks you); review color/size
   `valueChanges`.
4. `vp run upgrade:bless` + `vp run sync:compatibility`; commit; open the PR (report as the body).
5. CI's `upstream-drift` job posts the summary and enforces the blessed baseline; changesets and the
   compatibility gate enforce the rest. Optionally add a scheduled weekly workflow that re-resolves the
   pins and opens a Renovate-style PR when `summary.total > 0`.

## Verification

- Unit: `tools/upstream-diff/src` tests (bucket classification, icon-rename detection, per-theme diff,
  category routing); a fixture ledger through `deprecationShims` asserting a `var()` shim token appears
  in the IR with `meta.deprecated`; `generate-compatibility` / `check-compatibility` round-trip.
- Integration: `vp run ready` (build, `vp check`, `test -r`, css/js lint, `validate:generated:only`,
  the new `gate:token-drift` + `gate:compatibility`, markdown lint) and `vp run check:publish` both
  green. `vp run upgrade:check` produces a non-empty v1.4.0→v1.5.0 report.
- Consumer smoke: build `platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`, and
  `renderers/react-markdown` at the new pins; confirm no new dangling/unknown refs and that
  react-markdown still renders against ui-* `^11.7.4`.
- CI: open the upgrade PR; confirm the `upstream-drift` job posts the sticky comment, uploads the
  report, and enforces the blessed baseline.

## Open risks / watch-items

- **Provenance can't trust `package.json.version`** (stuck at `1.0.0`); derive from the pin ref +
  lockfile commit. This is the single most error-prone spot.
- **Baseline bootstrapping** (step F3): the very first `upgrade:check` needs a pre-bump baseline to be
  meaningful.
- **`github:#tag` resolution** in pnpm produces a tarball-commit lockfile entry; confirm `vp install`
  pins deterministically and the CI paths-filter watches both `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the lockfile.
- **Node-free browser graphs:** keep the new tooling (`tools/upstream-diff`, release scripts) out of
  `@pantoken/components` / `@pantoken/web-components` runtime imports — they're build/CI only.

input.content:
# @pantoken/upstream-diff

The upstream-drift gate. It projects the built token IR (every theme, plus the icon set) into a
compact, committed manifest, then classifies what an Instructure UI bump changed against that
baseline — added, removed, retyped, and re-referenced tokens, and added, removed, renamed, or changed
icons — into review buckets, and flags the subset that needs a human.

```sh
vp run upgrade:check   # diff current build vs baseline; write the report; fail on unblessed drift
vp run upgrade:bless   # rewrite the baseline from the current build (accept a reviewed bump)
```

The baseline (`baseline/manifest.json`) is committed and behaves like a lockfile: the gate fails when
it doesn't match the current build, so a PR that bumps the upstream pin must bless the baseline in the
same change. That surfaces every token and icon delta in the PR diff and in the printed report
(`generated/report.md`, `report.json`).

Reference integrity (dangling / unknown `var()` refs) is gated separately by
`@pantoken/validate-generated`, so this tool stays focused on token and icon drift.

content.text: Now add the paths-filtered `upstream-drift` CI job (mirroring the `docs-changes`/`docs` split) and register it in `ci-gate`:

input.old_string:
# Detect docs-relevant changes so PRs only pay for the docs build when the site could change. Runs on
  # both events (never skipped) so the `docs` job's `needs` is always satisfied.
  docs-changes:
input.new_string:
# Detect changes that could shift the vendored token IR, so the upstream-drift gate runs only when a
  # bump (or the pipeline itself) changed. Runs on both events so `upstream-drift`'s `needs` resolves.
  upstream-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      upstream: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.upstream }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Detect upstream-pin changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            upstream:
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - 'formats/tokens/**'
              - 'tools/upstream-diff/**'

  # The upstream-drift gate: fails when the committed baseline doesn't match the freshly built token IR,
  # forcing a bump to be blessed (`vp run upgrade:bless`) in the same PR. The classified report is printed
  # to the job log and uploaded as an artifact so every token/icon delta is visible on the PR.
  upstream-drift:
    needs: [build, upstream-changes]
    if: needs.upstream-changes.outputs.upstream == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Check upstream drift
        run: vp run upgrade:check
      - name: Upload drift report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: upstream-drift-report
          path: tools/upstream-diff/generated
          retention-days: 7

  # Detect docs-relevant changes so PRs only pay for the docs build when the site could change. Runs on
  # both events (never skipped) so the `docs` job's `needs` is always satisfied.
  docs-changes:

for deprecation / removal we should take things that are deprecated/dropped in instructure/ui* or instructure-design-tokens patches (Major.Minor.Patch) and mark them as `deprecated` but keep support until the next minor release.  So if 11.7.4 drops something, we mark it as 'deprected' until 11.8.0 drops, and then we cut a minor version of the consumer to.  So 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4 (deprecated) -> 0.2.0 (removed) for example.  If new deprecations are introduced in 11.8.0 (for example) then our 0.2.0 marks them as deprecated until 11.9.0 or 12.0.0.  This allows us to auto-document when a thing is deprecated, and indicate when it will be removed - by minor version.  Our minor versions can still move on their own so if we had already moved to 0.2.0 and then additional deprecations were added that would move us to 0.2.1 and then 11.8.0 would move us to 0.3.0, for example.

That reshapes the deprecation model significantly — a proper lifecycle, not a static alias/removed flag. Let me restate it back to be sure I build the right thing:

- Something dropped upstream in a **patch** (11.7.4) → we mark it **deprecated** and **keep a working shim**, tracking **when it was deprecated** and **the upstream minor that will remove it** (11.8.0).
- At that removal minor, we **drop the shim and cut a consumer minor** (0.1.4 deprecated → 0.2.0 removed). Consumer minors still move independently.
- The ledger drives **auto-documentation**: "deprecated in X, removal in Y."

This changes the ledger entry from a static `policy` to a `{ deprecatedIn, removeIn }` lifecycle, and it means the removal step must be *enforced* (a gate that fails once `removeIn` is reached until the entry is retired). Let me confirm two design points before I build the enforcement, since they change the machinery:

questions.question: When the removal minor is reached (e.g. upstream hits 11.8.0), how hard should the pipeline push the removal?

options.label: Hard-fail bless until retired
options.description: `upgrade:bless` refuses to accept a bump at/after a deprecation's removeIn until that ledger entry is retired (shim dropped). Forces the 0.2.0 removal + consumer minor exactly at the boundary. Strongest guarantee; can't drift.

options.label: Warn + report only
options.description: The drift report and a gate log flag "N deprecations due for removal" but don't block. The maintainer chooses when to cut the removal minor. Lower friction, but a shim can outlive its window.

questions.question: For a dropped token with no clean replacement (e.g. badge-notification-z-index = 1), how should the shim keep support during the deprecation window?

options.label: Freeze last-known value
options.description: The shim re-emits the token's last value from the pre-bump baseline (e.g. `: 1`), so behavior is unchanged until removal. Entries may carry either a `replacement` (→ var(...)) or a frozen `value`.

options.label: Require a replacement always
options.description: Every deprecation must forward to an existing canonical token; a drop with no sensible replacement is hard-removed immediately (no shim). Simpler ledger, but can't preserve a value that has no equivalent.

/**

 * @param  {Object} theme The actual theme object.

const generateComponentTheme = (theme: Theme): TruncateTextTheme => {

  const componentVariables: TruncateTextTheme = {

---
name: instui-upgrade-pipeline
description: The reusable Instructure UI upgrade pipeline — drift diff, token deprecation lifecycle, and consumer compatibility manifest
metadata:

---

pantoken has a semi-automated pipeline for upgrading its upstream Instructure UI sources, built
2026-07-24 during the 11.7.4 / design-tokens v1.5.0 bump. See [[pantoken-architecture]].

**Upstream surface (verified):** pantoken never depends on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package. Three
tiers, all pinned in the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog: `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens`
(GitHub-only, now pinned to a **release tag** `#v1.5.0`, feeds the token IR via `packages/core/src/build.ts`);
`@instructure/ui-icons` (feeds icons via `packages/core/src/icons.ts`); and eight `@instructure/ui-*`
React packages (consumed ONLY by `renderers/react-markdown`). Ingestion blast radius = those two core files.

**Provenance gotcha:** the design-tokens repo's `package.json` version is STUCK at `1.0.0` across every
tag, so provenance must record the pinned tag + the lockfile commit, never `package.json.version`.
`formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` writes `generated/meta.json` = `{designTokens:{ref,commit}, uiIcons:{resolved}}`,
exposed at `@pantoken/tokens/meta` (and re-exported from `./raw`).

**Drift gate — `tools/upstream-diff` (`@pantoken/upstream-diff`, private):** `lib.ts` projects the built
IR into a compact committed baseline `baseline/manifest.json` (per-theme token snapshots + hashed icon set;
~2MB — the "compact" form vs ~13MB full IR) and classifies a diff into buckets (added/removed/value/
syntax/ref token changes; added/removed/renamed/changed icons — rename = matching artwork hash). Runner
`index.ts`: `vp run upgrade:check` (fails on unblessed drift, writes `generated/report.{md,json}`),
`vp run upgrade:bless` (rewrites baseline). CI job `upstream-drift` in ci.yml is paths-filtered on
pnpm-workspace.yaml/pnpm-lock.yaml/formats-tokens/tools-upstream-diff. NOT in ready:all (would fire on
routine core-output changes). Reference-integrity stays gated by `validate-generated` (not duplicated here).

**Deprecation lifecycle — `plugins/pantoken/deprecations` (`@pantoken/plugin-deprecations`) + ledger
`formats/tokens/deprecations.json`:** when upstream drops a token, add a ledger entry
`{token, deprecatedIn, removeIn, replacement?|value?, note?}` (refs are `<tier>@<version>`, tier ∈
`ui`|`design-tokens`). `deprecationShims(ledger)` bakes a shim per entry into the vendored IR — a
`var(replacement)` forward OR a frozen last-known `value`. Kept working until `removeIn` upstream minor is
adopted, then the entry is RETIRED (shim dropped) and a consumer minor is cut. Enforced HARD in bless:
(1) dropping a real upstream token requires a ledger entry (coverage); a dropped token that was itself a
shim is exempt (retirement, not unhandled removal); (2) `dueForRemoval` — once current upstream ≥ removeIn,
bless fails until the entry is retired. Applied in generate.ts as a POST-build step (not `buildTokens({plugins})`)
to avoid the icons-stage "no icons hook" warning.

**Compatibility manifest — root `compatibility.json` + `docs/compatibility.md`:** writer/gate pair
`scripts/release/{generate,check}-compatibility.ts` (+ `compatibility.ts`), mirroring sync:/gate:repository.
Records the two upstream tiers (token-ir/icons vs instui-react), consumers (derived by scanning
renderers/* + platforms/* for `@instructure/*` deps — react-markdown is the sole instui-react consumer),
and the deprecation lifecycle table. `gate:compatibility` (parse-compare, formatting-agnostic) is in
ready:all; `sync:compatibility` regenerates. `docs/compatibility.md` is a top-level page — NOT scanned by
the locale parity/drift checks (those only cover docs/guide, docs/api, docs/index.md).

**Ingestion fix this bump:** ui-icons 11.7.4 moved onto lucide-react@1.23.0 whose ESM is `.mjs`
(was `.js` at 1.7.0). `icons.ts` `readEsmModule()` now tolerates both extensions.

**Future-bump runbook:** bump catalog pin → `vp install` → rebuild core+tokens → `vp run upgrade:check`
(read the classified report) → author deprecations.json entries for removed tokens (or bless refuses) →
`vp run upgrade:bless` + `vp run sync:compatibility` → changeset → PR (CI upstream-drift enforces the
blessed baseline).

That's the smoking gun. Look at `headBranch`: `@pantoken/pantoken@0.1.7`, `@pantoken/webpack@0.1.3`, … — those are **release tags**, not branches. The release creates ~30 package tags, each fires a `push` event, and there's a well-known GitHub quirk: **`paths` filters are ignored for tag pushes**. So the `push: paths:` trigger runs on every tag → the workflow fires ~30 times per release, doing nothing but `vp --version`.

What it's actually *for*: it's the GitHub Copilot coding agent's environment-setup file (and this repo has `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so Copilot is configured). GitHub invokes the `copilot-setup-steps` job **directly** when provisioning the agent — it doesn't rely on the `on:` triggers at all. The `push`/`pull_request` triggers exist only to validate the file when it changes, and `pull_request` already covers that. So the `push` trigger is both redundant and the sole cause of the spam.

The surgical fix: drop the `push` trigger. Let me branch and make it:

Done — [PR #41](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/41) is open.

**Diagnosis:** it wasn't the release *event* triggering it — it was the release *tags*. The workflow had `push: paths: [copilot-setup-steps.yml]`, and GitHub **ignores `paths` filters for tag pushes**. So each of the ~30 package release tags (`@pantoken/…@vX.Y.Z`) matched the `push` trigger and ran the job — which does nothing but `vp --version`. The run history confirmed it: every run's `headBranch` was a release tag, not a branch.

**You're right that it does nothing on release** — but the file itself isn't useless: it's the GitHub Copilot coding agent's environment-setup file (this repo has `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so Copilot is configured). GitHub runs the `copilot-setup-steps` **job** directly when provisioning the agent, independent of the `on:` triggers.

**Fix:** dropped the `push` trigger only. Copilot still gets its setup job, `pull_request` still validates the file when it changes, and `workflow_dispatch` still allows manual runs — but release tags no longer spam it. No changeset needed (no package source changed).

If you've actually retired the Copilot coding agent entirely, the alternative is deleting `copilot-setup-steps.yml` (and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) outright — say the word and I'll swap this PR for that.

content.text:
Fixed — [PR #42](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/42) is open.

**Why it failed:** I set `@pantoken/plugin-deprecations` up as a public package (modeled on the other plugins), but a brand-new public `@pantoken/*` package has no npm trusted publisher configured, so the OIDC publish fails. And it shouldn't be published anyway — its shims are baked into `@pantoken/tokens` at build time, so it's build-time-only tooling like `@pantoken/upstream-diff` and `@pantoken/validate-generated`.

**Fix:** marked it `private: true` and dropped the npm-page fields (`publishConfig`, `homepage`, `bugs`, `repository`). Kept `exports` + `files` so `@pantoken/tokens` and `@pantoken/upstream-diff` still resolve it in-workspace — and so publint stays clean (it flags `exports` pointing at `dist` when `dist` isn't in `files`).

**Verified:** the plugin still builds, `@pantoken/tokens` still bakes the shims (4,639 tokens), `gate:repository` now checks 68 publishable packages (was 69), publint says "All good!", and `vp run check:publish` is fully green. No changeset needed since it's no longer publishable.

The stale `@pantoken/plugin-deprecations@0.2.0` git tag from the failed release is harmless — nothing published at that version, and future releases will skip the package. Once #42 merges, the release stops trying to publish it.
